program.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
requirements.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edited images, what does the visual evidence establish about the requested move of the source mug to the right of the headphones: complete fulfillment, partial progress, no progress, or unresolved?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself was moved and is now to the right of the same headphones. Fail only if evidence reliably establishes that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. Treat as partial progress when the edited image provides credible visual evidence of an attempted or incomplete move of the source mug, even if its identity or final position is uncertain—for example, a conspicuous mug-shaped remnant or blur at its former location together with a mug on the right. Do not treat uncertainty about whether a right-side mug is the source mug as proof of no progress, and do not infer complete fulfillment from a right-side mug alone. Use unknown when the evidence cannot reliably establish either relevant progress or no progress, or cannot determine whether the requested condition is fulfilled.
nodes.binding: Cross-image binding: the source blue mug and the same headphones in the source and edited images. Compare the source mug with all visible edited mugs, assess their left-to-right positions relative to the headphones, and inspect the source mug’s former location for evidence of a remnant or movement, allowing for changes in scale, lighting, and appearance.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1: The trace’s evidence supports partial progress, not its emitted `yes`: the edited image shows a conspicuous blue mug-shaped remnant at the source location and a mug to the right of the headphones, but the right-side mug does not visibly match the source blue mug, and the headphones also appear altered. The binding currently asks to compare the source mug with edited mugs, yet the trace treats the right-side mug as the moved source mug and concludes fulfillment. Tighten the decision criterion so it distinguishes evidence of an attempted move from reliable identity and final-position evidence: a remnant plus a right-side mug can support partial progress without establishing that the source mug itself is now correctly placed. Preserve `unknown` when the visual evidence cannot resolve fulfillment; do not convert uncertainty into either no progress or complete success. Check the node’s label mapping/routing as well: its trace says the move is only toward the right while the aggregate emits `yes` against a `partial` reference. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported.

observations.evidence: The source shows a blue mug to the left of the headphones. In the edited image, a mug is clearly positioned to the right of the headphones, and the source mug’s former left-side location has a conspicuous blue, mug-shaped blur/remnant. Together these provide evidence that the source mug was moved toward the right; the right-side mug is beyond the headphones.

findings.source_phrase: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
findings.question: Does the edited image reliably establish that the mug to the right of the headphones is the source blue mug, rather than a different mug, and that it is positioned to the right of the same headphones?
findings.criteria: Inspect the edited mugs’ appearance and the headphones’ identity and position against the source. A mug on the right alone does not establish that the source mug was moved there; distinguish evidence of the source mug’s identity from evidence of movement.
findings.evidence: The source has one large blue mug left of the headphones. The edited image shows a blue mug-shaped blur at the former location, a small light-colored mug left of the headphones, and another light-colored mug to their right. The right-side mug is visibly to the right, but its correspondence to the source blue mug is not established by the observation’s claim of a remnant alone.
findings.rationale: The existing broad check passes based on the claimed blur/remnant and right-side mug, but the edited image contains multiple mugs and the right-side mug differs visibly in color and scale from the source mug. A focused identity-and-relation check is needed to assess whether the requested source mug itself is now right of the headphones, without treating uncertainty as proof of no progress.
